summary: Phase 9C frontend testing PASSED. All six Phase 9C requirements verified: (1) Sidebar 'Public chats' search section appears for query 'lam' and renders matching public chats via /api/discover, (2) clicking a public-chat search result opens the PublicChatPreviewDrawer with correct title/handle/count/description/primary-action, (3) Join button calls POST /api/conversations/join, closes drawer, and activates the conversation, (4) /c/handle mentions in message bubbles route through the drawer (mention-conv-<handle>), (5) close button AND desktop backdrop click both remove the drawer, (6) group typing names render with chat-header-group-typing in single ('Bob is typing') and two-person ('Charlie and Bob are typing') formats and revert to chat-header-group-members when typing stops.

minor.issue: In group conversations the typing event is only broadcast to a single recipient: `other_id = next((p for p in conv['participants'] if p != user_id), None)`. This is the DM logic; for groups every non-sender participant should receive the typing event. Currently only the first non-sender participant in the participants array can see typing names. The frontend label code is correct; this backend bug silently limits the feature to one lucky recipient per group. Recommendation: iterate over all non-sender participants.

issues: Spec asked for 'Join channel' / 'Join group', but the rendered label is 'Join this channel'. Behaviour is correct; only the i18n string wording differs. Minor copy nit, not blocking.

action_items: Fix backend group typing routing (server.py ~L2593): broadcast typing event to ALL non-sender participants, not just the first one returned by next(...). This is required for the Phase 9C group typing names feature to work for every group member.
Optional: review i18n keys for drawer primary action — current label 'Join this channel' vs spec wording 'Join channel'.

Optional: investigate console error 'React does not recognize the `%s` prop on a DOM element ... didFire didfire' that fires on app load; appears to be a framer-motion DOM attribute leak (non-blocking).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L2585-L2600: typing handler uses next() which is DM-only logic but the comment/structure doesn't gate by conversation kind — silently breaks group typing.
PublicChatPreviewDrawer hook usage is solid; drawer correctly closes on join success and backdrop click.
seed_data_creation: Sent two messages from alice → bob DM (client_ids TEST_mention_9c, TEST_mention_9c_2, TEST_mention_conv_v3) to validate mention parsing. Existing public channel handle 'lama' (kind=channel) used for drawer + join tests; existing group 23ba6d1c-1972-4370-b5c6-ca552867d569 (alice+bob+charlie+1 other) used for typing tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 9C frontend wiring is fully working. The only non-trivial finding is a backend bug in the WebSocket typing handler that limits group typing broadcasts to a single recipient — confirmed via direct WS connection from bob+charlie while alice viewed the group; alice received both events only because she happens to be the first non-sender participant in conv.participants. Other members of the same group would not see the typing label. Mention routing requires the '/c/handle' syntax (not '@handle') to be tagged as type='conv' in parseMentions.js — '@lama' is correctly parsed as a user mention and remains so unless prefixed with '/c/'. Drawer behaviour, search section, join flow and close interactions all verified pixel-by-pixel with screenshots.
rca of the issue: Group typing single-recipient bug RCA: server.py uses `other_id = next((p for p in conv['participants'] if p != user_id), None)` regardless of conversation kind. For DMs this resolves to the lone peer. For groups it picks only the first non-sender participant, dropping the typing event for every other group member. Mitigation: replace with `for other_id in conv['participants']: if other_id != user_id: await manager.send_to_user(other_id, payload)`.
